target.title: fix(browser): preserve strict CDP discovery policy on target-list lookup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the browser plugin resolves a page by target id over a remote CDP
endpoint, `findPageByTargetId` falls back to the CDP `/json/list` target list
(`findPageByTargetIdViaTargetList`) whenever per-page CDP probing cannot map the
target. That fallback fetched `/json/list` without applying the caller's CDP
discovery policy, so a configured endpoint's host-scoping was not enforced on
that one lookup — the same `/json/list` fetch that the sibling terminate path
already scopes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This completes the strict CDP discovery policy preservation that
`7d0f9de907` ("preserve strict CDP discovery policy") applied to the sibling
`tryTerminateExecutionViaCdp`, for the remaining same-shaped `/json/list`
lookup path. `findPageByTargetIdViaTargetList` now builds the scoped control
policy with `scopeCdpPolicyToConfiguredEndpoint(cdpUrl, ssrfPolicy)` and passes
it to `fetchJson`, so the target-list lookup enforces the configured endpoint's
host scope like the other CDP fetch paths in the plugin
(`cdp.ts`, `chrome.ts`, `chrome.diagnostics.ts`, `server-context.tab-ops.ts`,
and the sibling terminate path). This lookup does not connect to a discovered
`webSocketDebuggerUrl` (it matches by id only), so no discovered-source
assertion is added.

## User Impact

No change to successful page resolution: the target-list fallback still returns
the matching page for a configured endpoint. Operators running the browser
plugin against a remote CDP endpoint now get the same discovery-policy scoping
on the `/json/list` target-list lookup that the other CDP paths already apply.

## Evidence

Focused tests, run with
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session.target-list-cdp-ssrf.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session.termination-cdp-ssrf.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session.get-page-for-targetid.extension-fallback.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.test.ts`:

- `pw-session.target-list-cdp-ssrf.test.ts` (new) — drives the production
  `getPageForTargetId` target-list fallback and asserts the caller's discovery
  policy reaches the `/json/list` fetch guard (host-scoped allowlist + the
  caller's policy flags preserved). Reverting the one-line fix fails this test.
- Sibling suites unaffected: `pw-session.termination-cdp-ssrf.test.ts`,
  `pw-session.get-page-for-targetid.extension-fallback.test.ts`,
  `cdp.helpers.test.ts` — 38 tests pass together with the new test.

Additional manual boundary capture (a standalone script, not part of the
committed test suite) exercising the real fetch-guard stack (production
`fetchJson` → `fetchCdpChecked` → SSRF guard, no mocks; served by a local
`/json/list` HTTP server):

```
configured cdpUrl: http://127.0.0.1:<port>
strict caller policy: {"dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork":false,"allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange":true}

[before] fetchJson policy arg  = undefined
[before] /json/list reachable  = [{"id":"TARGET_B","url":"https://beta.example"}]

[after]  cdpControlPolicy       = {"dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork":false,"allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange":true,"allowedHostnames":["127.0.0.1"],"hostnameAllowlist":["127.0.0.1"]}
[after]  /json/list reachable   = [{"id":"TARGET_B","url":"https://beta.example"}]
[after]  allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange preserved = true
[after]  authority-deviating fetch (169.254.169.254) blocked = true

RESULT: PASS
```

Before the change the fetch received no policy argument; after it, the scoped
control policy reaches the guard, the configured-host lookup still succeeds, and
an authority-deviating fetch is blocked by the scoped policy.
